newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: SOCCER-EL SALVADOR DENY COACH HAS RESIGNED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EL SALVADOR DENY COACH HAS RESIGNED.

text.p: El Salvador soccer bosses have denied that Milovan D'Joric had resigned as coach of the country's trouble-hit national team.
"We haven't heard anything from him, neither verbal nor in writing," Juan Torres, president of the country's soccer federation, said on Thursday.
Confusion had reigned since Wednesday when radio stations read what they claimed was D'Joric's letter of resignation.
But the coach said on Thursday he was still in charge. "I still haven't resigned. One thing is to pack your suitcase, another is to resign."
D'Joric had reportedly been upset at the inclusion of two players he did not pick at national team training sessions.

Four players from the Alianza club abandoned training on Monday, claiming they were being overworked, while the coach was also reported to have had a blazing row with a team official who was sacked but later reinstated.

El Salvador have reached the final six-team stage of the CONCACAF region World Cup qualifying competition, which is led by Mexico and which provides three finalists for next year's tournament in France.

But a home defeat against Mexico, a draw at home to the United States and a loss in Jamaica seem to have wrecked their chances of a third appearance at the finals. Their next game is away to Costa Rica on August 10.
